answer: Hardware-bound admission requires each agent to run inside a physical vault that signs a cryptographic thread every millisecond using its factory-fused key. A network lantern audits each incoming thread for memory-bus latency and clock-skew covariance, counting how many virtualized identities share the same silicon die. The $m$-th agent executing on the same vault must lock $20m$ FIL into the lantern to stay active. An honest operator with one agent locks 20 FIL, while an attacker packing $n$ sybils onto one vault locks $10n(n+1)$ FIL or buys $n$ separate physical machines.
